reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

votes.question: On Passage — Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008)
votes.bill_title: Stop Insider Trading Act
votes.plain_language: This bill generally bars members of Congress and their spouses and dependent children from buying stocks, and it requires public notice before they sell. A Yea passes it in the House. A Nay votes against passage.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008)
votes.bill_title: Stop Insider Trading Act
votes.plain_language: The Stop Insider Trading Act would bar members of Congress and their spouses and dependent children from buying stocks and would require public notice before a sale. This vote would have replaced that bill with a broader ban that also forces members, the President, the Vice President, and their spouses and dependent children to sell covered investments they already hold. A Yea would have made that swap; a Nay kept the original bill.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027 (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: The fiscal year 2027 defense bill sets military policy, troop levels, and related Energy Department security programs. This vote would have sent that bill back to the Armed Services Committee with no rewrite attached. A Yea would have pulled it off the floor; a Nay left it up for the passage vote.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment would have required the Defense Secretary to report options for cutting the department's civilian workforce by 200,000. A Yea would have added that report. A Nay voted not to add it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to the fiscal year 2027 defense bill would ban automated speed-enforcement cameras on military bases. A Yea adds that ban to the bill. A Nay leaves the bill without it.

votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) would have let the Secretary approve any eligible investor and cleared investment professional who meets the program's requirements to assess investment opportunities matching the department's needs, with no cap on participants, according to the Congressional Research Service description. A Yea supports adopting it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027

This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Community Bank Deposit Access Act (H R 5317)
votes.bill_title: Community Bank Deposit Access Act of 2025
votes.plain_language: This bill changes the treatment of certain types of deposits so they are no longer classified as brokered deposits. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — American Access to Banking Act (H R 4544)
votes.bill_title: American Access to Banking Act
votes.plain_language: This bill requires federal financial regulators to review and streamline the application process for the formation of de novo, or new, depository institutions or credit unions. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Keeping Deposits Local Act (H R 3234)
votes.bill_title: Keeping Deposits Local Act
votes.plain_language: This bill increases the amount insured depository institutions may accept as reciprocal deposits. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Whistleblower Protection Act (H R 4646)
votes.bill_title: Whistleblower Protection Act of 2025
votes.plain_language: This bill extends whistleblower protections to employees of Housing and Urban Development contractors and grantees, including on contracts signed before 2013. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Concur in Senate Adt to House Adt to Senate Adt — Housing for the 21st Century Act (H R 6644)
votes.bill_title: 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act
votes.plain_language: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act establishes and modifies various federal housing programs. This vote, under suspension of the rules, was on accepting the Senate's latest changes to the bill after the chambers traded versions, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea accepts the Senate's version; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Agree — Providing for the concurrence by the House in the Senate amendment to H.R. 6644, with amendment (H RES 1299)
votes.bill_title: Providing for the concurrence by the House in the Senate amendment to H.R. 6644, with amendment.
votes.plain_language: The official title of H.Res. 1299 is “Providing for the concurrence by the House in the Senate amendment to H.R. 6644, with amendment.” No official summary was available. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports agreeing to it; a Nay opposes it.

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.

town_halls.note: There is no national town-hall dataset. Dates are not estimated.

disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
vote_scope: This is not a full career record. The cache is the latest 40 House rolls (2026, rolls 275-314) and 40 Senate votes (119th Congress, session 2, votes 217-256).
